The '''70th Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), took place on March 23, 1998, at the [[Shrine Auditorium]] in [[Los Angeles]] beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the show, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 24 categories honoring [[1997 in film|films released in 1997]]. The ceremony, which was televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Gilbert Cates|Gil Cates]] and directed by Louis J. Horvitz.<ref>{{cite news|last=Snow |first=Shauna |title=Arts and entertainment reports from The Times, national and international news services and the nation's press. |url=https://articles.latimes.com/1997/dec/12/entertainment/ca-63145/2 |access-date=January 26, 2014 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 12, 1997 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222171218/http://articles.latimes.com/1997/dec/12/entertainment/ca-63145/2 |archive-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Horvitz to helm Academy broadcast |url=https://variety.com/1998/more/news/jan-8-1998-1117434573/ |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |date=January 8, 1998 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131107092342/http://variety.com/1998/more/news/jan-8-1998-1117434573/ |archive-date=November 7, 2013}}</ref> Actor [[Billy Crystal]] hosted the show for the sixth time.<ref>{{cite news|title=Crystal set for sixth Oscar stint |url=https://variety.com/1997/more/news/dec-21-1997-111799971/ |access-date=January 22, 2014 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]] |date=December 21, 1997 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140223205737/http://variety.com/1997/more/news/dec-21-1997-111799971/ |archive-date=February 23, 2014}}</ref> He had first hosted the [[62nd Academy Awards|62nd ceremony]] held in 1990, and most recently the [[69th Academy Awards|previous year's awards]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Crowe |first=Jerry |title=Arts and entertainment reports from The Times, national and international news services and the nation's press. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-dec-20-ca-382-story.html |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=December 20, 1997 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131106065228/http://articles.latimes.com/1997/dec/20/entertainment/ca-382 |archive-date=November 6, 2013}}</ref> Nearly a month earlier in an event held at the [[Beverly Wilshire Hotel|Regent Beverly Wilshire Hotel]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]] on February 28, the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by host [[Ashley Judd]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Judd named presenter at 70th Oscars |url=https://variety.com/1998/more/news/from-feb-20-1117467952/ |access-date=January 24, 2014 |work=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |date=February 20, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226132326/http://variety.com/1998/more/news/from-feb-20-1117467952/ |archive-date=February 26, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]'' won 11 awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], a number that is tied with ''[[Ben-Hur (1959 film)|Ben-Hur]]'' and ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King]]''.<ref>{{cite news|last=Harden|first=Mark|title=Epic film sails away with Oscar boatload|work=[[The Denver Post]]|publisher=[[MediaNews Group]]|page=A-01|date=March 24, 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Weinraub |first=Bernard |title='Titanic' Ties Record With 11 Oscars, Including Best Picture |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/03/24/movies/titanic-ties-record-with-11-oscars-including-best-picture.html |access-date=January 25, 2014 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 24, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131226202302/http://www.nytimes.com/1998/03/24/movies/titanic-ties-record-with-11-oscars-including-best-picture.html |archive-date=December 26, 2013}}</ref> Other winners included ''[[As Good as It Gets]]'', ''[[Good Will Hunting]]'', and ''[[L.A. Confidential (film)|L.A. Confidential]]'' with two awards, and ''[[Character (film)|Character]]'', ''[[The Full Monty]]'', ''[[Geri's Game]]'', ''[[The Long Way Home (1997 film)|The Long Way Home]]'', ''[[Men in Black (1997 film)|Men in Black]]'', ''[[A Story of Healing]]'', and ''[[Visas and Virtue]]'' with one. The telecast garnered more than 57 million viewers in the United States, making it the most-watched Oscars broadcast in history.<ref>{{cite news|last=Scanton |first=Julian |title=Could Avatar Boost Oscar Ratings to Record Heights? |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/online/oscars/2010/01/could-avatar-boost-oscar-ratings-to-record-heights |access-date=March 12, 2014 |work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |publisher=[[Condé Nast]] |date=January 27, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312224910/http://www.vanityfair.com/online/oscars/2010/01/could-avatar-boost-oscar-ratings-to-record-heights |archive-date=March 12, 2014}}</ref>

==Winners and nominees==
<!--Please do not add any fact or statement below unless you have a credible source verifying it. Otherwise, it will be promptly removed.-->

The nominees for the 70th Academy Awards were announced on February 10, 1998, at the Samuel Goldwyn Theater in Beverly Hills, California, by [[Robert Rehme]], president of the academy, and actress [[Geena Davis]].<ref name="cnnnom">{{cite news|title='Titanic' cruises into Oscars lead |url=http://www.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9802/10/oscar.nominations/ |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=[[CNN]] |publisher=[[Time Warner]] |date=February 10, 1998 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103083024/http://www.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9802/10/oscar.nominations/ |archive-date=November 3, 2013}}</ref> ''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]'' led all nominees with fourteen nominations, tying with ''[[All About Eve]]'' (1950) for the most Oscar nominations in history.{{efn|Subsequently, ''[[La La Land]]'' (2016) received 14 nominations at the [[89th Academy Awards]]. The tied record was broken by ''[[Sinners (2025 film)|Sinners]]'' (2025), which received 16 nominations at the [[98th Academy Awards]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/sinners-most-nominated-movie-oscars-history-2026-1236480942/ |title='Sinners' Gets Most Oscar Nominations Ever |last=Canfield |first=David |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=January 22, 2026 |access-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260124013816/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/sinners-most-nominated-movie-oscars-history-2026-1236480942/ |archive-date=January 24, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>}} ''[[Good Will Hunting]]'' and ''[[L.A. Confidential (film)|L.A. Confidential]]'' came in second with nine apiece.<ref>Multiple sources:
*{{cite news|last=Ebert|first=Roger|title=Oscar hopefuls"Titanic' ties a record; DiCaprio misses boat|work=The Denver Post|publisher=MediaNews Group|page=F-01|date=February 10, 1998}}
*{{cite news|title='Titanic' lands 14 Oscar nominations; ties 1950 record|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|publisher=Tribune Publishing|page=A-3|date=February 11, 1998}}
*{{cite news |last1=Waxman |first1=Sharon |title='TITANIC' TOPS OSCARS LIST |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1998/02/11/titanic-tops-oscars-list/64513d8a-c1e3-4dc5-b663-c97e4cbc0245/ |access-date=March 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170827043502/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1998/02/11/titanic-tops-oscars-list/64513d8a-c1e3-4dc5-b663-c97e4cbc0245/ |archive-date=August 27, 2017| newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 10, 1998 |url-status=live }}
</ref>

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 23, 1998. With eleven awards, ''Titanic'' tied with ''[[Ben-Hur (1959 film)|Ben-Hur]]'' (1959) for the most Academy Awards in Oscar history.<ref>{{cite news|last=Goldsten |first=Patrick |title='Titanic' Snags 11, Ties for Record |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-mar-24-mn-32150-story.html |access-date=January 25, 2014 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 24, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205031141/http://articles.latimes.com/1998/mar/24/news/mn-32150 |archive-date=December 5, 2013}}</ref>{{efn|name=Tie2|''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King]]'' (2003) has since equaled this record with eleven wins.<ref>{{cite news|last=Smith |first=Neil |title=Rings joins Oscar's big winners |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/3521401.stm |access-date=July 8, 2013 |work=[[BBC News]] |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=March 1, 2004 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105110109/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/3521401.stm |archive-date=November 5, 2013 }}</ref>}} It also became the first film to win Best Picture without a screenwriting nomination since ''[[The Sound of Music (film)|The Sound of Music]]'' (1965).<ref>{{cite news|last=Guthmann |first=Edward |title='Titanic' Rides an Oscar Tidal Wave / But Hunt and Nicholson take the top acting awards |url=http://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Titanic-Rides-an-Oscar-Tidal-Wave-But-Hunt-3011161.php |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |publisher=[[Hearst Corporation]] |date=March 24, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103212932/http://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Titanic-Rides-an-Oscar-Tidal-Wave-But-Hunt-3011161.php |archive-date=November 3, 2013}}</ref> Due to ''Titanic'', [[James Cameron]] became the first person to win as a producer, director and editor in one night.<ref name="Variety">{{cite news|last=Gray |first=Tim |title=‘Titanic’ tally ties Oscar record |url=https://variety.com/1998/more/news/titanic-tally-ties-oscar-record-2-1117469068/ |access-date=May 24, 2026 |newspaper=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=March 22, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106061819/http://variety.com/1998/more/news/titanic-tally-ties-oscar-record-2-1117469068/ |archive-date=January 6, 2015}}</ref> [[Jack Nicholson]] received his eleventh acting nomination, becoming the most nominated man in acting categories.<ref name="cnnnom"/> He also became the fourth performer to win at least [[List of actors with two or more Academy Awards in acting categories|three acting Oscars]].<ref name="Variety"/> Both Nicholson and [[Helen Hunt]] won for their roles in ''[[As Good as It Gets]]'', making it the seventh film to win both lead acting awards.<ref name="Variety"/> Nominated for their performances as Rose DeWitt Bukater in ''Titanic'', Best Actress nominee [[Kate Winslet]] and Best Supporting Actress nominee [[Gloria Stuart]] became the first pair of performers nominated for portraying the same character in the same film.<ref name="cnnnom"/> At the age of 87, Stuart became the [[List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees|oldest acting nominee]] in Oscars history.<ref>{{cite news |title=Titanic actress Gloria Stuart dies at 100 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-11423017 |access-date=June 20, 2026 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=September 27, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220135451/http://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-11423017 |archive-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref>

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Billy Crystal VF 2012 Shankbone.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Billy Crystal]] hosted the 70th Academy Awards.|alt=Photo of Billy Crystal in 2012.]]

In December 1997, the academy hired veteran Oscar telecast producer [[Gil Cates]] to oversee the 1998 ceremony.<ref name="Cates">{{cite news|last=Hindes |first=Andrew |title=And Cates makes eight |url=https://variety.com/1997/more/news/and-cates-makes-eight-1116680279/ |access-date=January 23, 2014 |work=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |date=December 11, 1997 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150404132631/http://variety.com/1997/more/news/and-cates-makes-eight-1116680279/ |archive-date=April 4, 2015}}</ref> "Gil has become the consummate Oscar show producer, consistently garnering top television ratings for the telecast," said AMPAS President Robert Rehme in a press release announcing the selection. "His shows are full of wit, charm and surprise."<ref name="Cates"/> A few days later, actor and comedian Billy Crystal was chosen to emcee the upcoming telecast. Cates explained his reason to bring back the veteran comedian saying, "Billy's performance last year was spectacular. There is nobody like him."<ref>{{cite news|title=News Lite Veteran DJ Will End Storied Career|work=Los Angeles Daily News|publisher=MediaNews Group|date=December 20, 1997|page=N2}}</ref> In an article published in ''[[USA Today]]'' he initially requested to Cates and AMPAS five months after the [[69th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]] that he would like to take a break from hosting duties. However, pressure from the academy, Cates, and several friends and family members made him reconsider his decision.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=156}}</ref> His sixth stint would make him second only to [[Bob Hope]] in number of ceremonies hosted.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=157}}</ref> For the first time, the show was procuded by AMPAS, not [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], because of the failure in reaching a contract agreement with the [[National Association of Broadcast Employees and Technicians]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Madigan |first=Nick |title=Sunday officially Oscar's |url=https://variety.com/1998/film/news/sunday-officially-oscar-s-1117477950/ |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Variety |date=June 26, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110222613/http://variety.com/1998/film/news/sunday-officially-oscar-s-1117477950/ |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref>

To commemorate the seventieth anniversary of the Academy Awards, 70 actors who have received both competitive and honorary awards appeared seated onstage together during a segment called Oscar's Family Album.<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|pp=185–186}}</ref> Each former winner was acknowledged by announcer [[Norman Rose]] with the films he or she won for. At the end of the segment newly minted winners Kim Basinger, Helen Hunt, and Robin Williams joined them. This marked the largest gathering of former winners since the [[50th Academy Awards|50th ceremony]] held in 1978.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=177}}</ref> The Academy also commissioned musician and composer [[Jerry Goldsmith]] to compose a new [[leitmotif]] for the Oscars telecast entitled "[[Fanfare for Oscar]]".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Karon |first=Paul |date=January 26, 1998 |title=Goldsmith pens official theme for academy awards |url=https://variety.com/1998/more/news/goldsmith-pens-official-theme-for-academy-awards-1117467118/ |access-date=March 10, 2025 |work=Variety |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205211617/https://variety.com/1998/more/news/goldsmith-pens-official-theme-for-academy-awards-1117467118/ |archive-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref>

Several others participated in the production of the ceremony. [[Bill Conti]] served as musical director for the telecast.<ref>{{cite news|title=Conti named musical director of 70th Academy Awards |url=https://variety.com/1998/more/news/jan-14-1998-1117436386/ |access-date=January 24, 2014 |work=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |date=January 14, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150404204359/https://variety.com/1998/more/news/jan-14-1998-1117436386/ |archive-date=April 4, 2015}}</ref> Dancer [[Daniel Ezralow]] choreographed a dance number showcasing the nominees for Best Original Comedy or Musical Score. [[Bart the Bear]] made a surprise appearance during the presentation of the [[Academy Award for Best Sound Editing|Best Sound Effects Editing]] award with [[Mike Myers]].<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|p=168}}</ref>

===Box office performance of nominees===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 10, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees was $579&nbsp;million with an average of $116&nbsp;million per film.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars>{{cite news|title=1997 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1997&p=.htm |access-date=November 2, 2013 |work=[[Box Office Mojo]]|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103203352/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1997&p=.htm |archive-date=November 3, 2013}}</ref> ''Titanic'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $338.7&nbsp;million in domestic box office receipts.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars/> The film was followed by ''As Good as It Gets'' ($92.6&nbsp;million), ''Good Will Hunting'' ($68.9&nbsp;million), ''L.A. Confidential'' ($39.7&nbsp;million), and finally ''The Full Monty'' ($38.7&nbsp;million).<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars/>

Of the top 50 grossing movies of the year, 40 nominations went to 15 films on the list. Only ''Titanic'' (1st), ''As Good as It Gets'' (16th), ''Good Will Hunting'' (20th), and ''In & Out'' (24th) were nominated for directing, acting, screenwriting, or Best Picture.<ref name="boxofficemojooscars">{{cite web|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1998-02-10&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1997&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |title=1997 Domestic Grosses|work=Box Office Mojo |access-date=June 5, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103210153/http://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1998-02-10&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1997&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=November 3, 2013}}</ref> The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were ''Men in Black'' (2nd), ''The Lost World: Jurassic Park'' (3rd), ''Air Force One'' (5th), ''My Best Friends Wedding'' (7th), ''Face/Off'' (9th), ''Con Air'' (12th), ''Contact'' (13th), ''Hercules'' (14th), ''The Fifth Element'' (25th), ''Anastasia'' (30th), and ''Starship Troopers'' (34th).<ref name="boxofficemojooscars" />

===Critical response===
The show received a positive reception from most media publications. Television critic [[Howard Rosenberg]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' lauded Crystal's performance writing that he "would earn top billing as that unusual comedian as artful at doing musical comedy as jokes."<ref>{{cite news|last=Rosenberg |first=Howard |title=Crystal Persuasion |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-mar-24-ca-32299-story.html |access-date=January 23, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 24, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221173400/http://articles.latimes.com/1998/mar/24/entertainment/ca-32299 |archive-date=February 21, 2014}}</ref> ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'' columnist John Carman raved,"It was the best Oscar show in two decades." He also gave high marks for the host, commenting, "But last night, Crystal was back in razor form."<ref>{{cite news|last=Carman |first=John |title=Oscar Polishes Up His Image / Crystal clearly a winner for best show in decades |url=http://www.sfgate.com/entertainment/article/Oscar-Polishes-Up-His-Image-Crystal-clearly-a-3011121.php |access-date=January 23, 2014 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |publisher=[[Hearst Corporation]] |date=March 24, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202225702/http://www.sfgate.com/entertainment/article/Oscar-Polishes-Up-His-Image-Crystal-clearly-a-3011121.php |archive-date=February 2, 2014}}</ref> ''[[The Seattle Times]]'' television editor Kay McFadden praised Crystal commenting that "he possesses nearly impeccable timing and judgment." In addition, she noted that while the ceremony dragged on, "Last night was one of television's smartest live ceremonies in recent memory."<ref>{{cite news|last=McFadden |first=Kay |title=Ceremony Shapes Up As A Night To Remember |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19980324/2741394/ceremony-shapes-up-as-a-night-to-remember |access-date=January 23, 2014 |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |publisher=[[The Seattle Times Company]] |date=March 24, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201200513/http://community.seattletimes.nwsource.com/archive/?date=19980324&slug=2741394 |archive-date=February 1, 2014}}</ref>

Some media outlets were more critical of the show. Ray Richmond of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' complained that the ceremony proved to be a "Yawner of an Oscarcast." He added that Crystal's "off-the-cuff one-liners sank faster than the great ship herself."<ref>{{cite news|last=Richmond |first=Ray |title=Review: 'The 70th Annual Academy Awards' |url=https://variety.com/1998/tv/reviews/the-70th-annual-academy-awards-1200453061/ |access-date=January 23, 2014 |work=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |date=March 23, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140225005701/http://variety.com/1998/tv/reviews/the-70th-annual-academy-awards-1200453061/ |archive-date=February 25, 2014}}</ref> ''[[Boston Globe]]'' television critic Matthew Gilbert bemoaned,"There was hardly a spontaneous moment during last night's Oscarcast."<ref>{{cite news|last=Gilbert|first=Matthew|title=Telecast Sinks Under Tired Bits, Little Spark|newspaper=Boston Globe|date=March 24, 1998|page=D1}}</ref> Film critic Carrie Rickey from ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' lamented that the inevitable ''Titanic'' sweep "sank a telecast loaded with montages of previous years' Oscar highlights."<ref>{{cite news|last=Rickey|first=Carey|title='Titanic' Ties Record With 11 Oscars; 'Good As It Gets' Takes Acting Honors|page=A1|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=[[Philadelphia Media Network]]|date=March 24, 1998}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 57.25 million people over its length, which was a 29% increase from the [[69th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Crupi |first=Anthony |title=ABC Strikes Gold With the Oscars |url=http://www.adweek.com/news/television/abc-strikes-gold-oscars-147081 |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=[[Adweek]] |publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]] |date=February 6, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103090449/http://www.adweek.com/news/television/abc-strikes-gold-oscars-147081 |archive-date=November 3, 2013}}</ref> An estimated 87.50 million total viewers watched all or part of the awards.<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|p=187}}</ref> The show also earned higher [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony with 35.32% of households watching over a 55.77 share.<ref name="TVB Oscars">{{cite news|title=Academy Awards ratings |work=Television Bureau of Advertising |url=https://www.tvb.org/Portals/0/media/file/tracts/Academy_Awards.pdf |access-date=June 27, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808235818/https://www.tvb.org/Portals/0/media/file/tracts/Academy_Awards.pdf |archive-date=August 8, 2016}}</ref> In addition, it garnered a higher 18{{ndash}}49 demo rating with a 24.90 rating over a 44.30 share among viewers in that demographic.<ref name="TVB Oscars" /> It was the most watched Oscar ceremony in television history since viewership figures were compiled beginning with the [[46th Academy Awards|46th ceremony]] in 1974.<ref>{{cite web |first=Bill |last=Gorman |title=Academy Awards Averages 41.3 Million Viewers; Most Since 2005 |url=http://tvbythenumbers.com/2010/03/08/academy-awards-averages-41-3-million-viewers-most-since-2005/44217 |work=[[TV by the Numbers]] |publisher=[[Tribune Media]] |date=March 8, 2010 |access-date=March 12, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100310080531/http://tvbythenumbers.com/2010/03/08/academy-awards-averages-41-3-million-viewers-most-since-2005/44217 |archive-date=March 10, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 1998, the ceremony presentation received eight nominations at the [[50th Primetime Emmy Awards|50th Primetime Emmys]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Primetime Emmy Award database |url=http://www.emmys.com/shows/70th-annual-academy-awards |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=[[Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] |publisher=ATAS |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121001085632/http://www.emmys.com/shows/70th-annual-academy-awards |archive-date=October 1, 2012}}</ref> Two months later, the ceremony won five of those nominations for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program|Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program]] (Billy Crystal), Outstanding Directing for a Variety or Music Program (Louis J Horvitz), Outstanding Lighting Direction (Electronic) for a Drama Series, Variety Series, Miniseries, or Movie (Bob Barnhart, Robert Dickinson, Matt Ford, Andy O'Reilly), Outstanding Music Direction (Bill Conti), and Outstanding Sound Mixing for a Variety Series or Special (Patrick Baltzell, Robert Douglass, Edward J. Greene, Tommy Vicari).<ref>{{cite news|title=The Emmy Winners Announced on Saturday |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-aug-31-ca-18105-story.html |access-date=November 1, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=August 31, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131106080823/http://articles.latimes.com/1998/aug/31/entertainment/ca-18105 |archive-date=November 6, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=1998 Emmy Winners |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/09/15/arts/the-1998-emmy-winners.html |access-date=November 2, 2013 |work=The New York Times |date=September 15, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114083821/http://www.nytimes.com/1998/09/15/arts/the-1998-emmy-winners.html |archive-date=November 14, 2013}}</ref>

=="In Memoriam"==
The annual "In Memoriam" tribute was presented by actress [[Whoopi Goldberg]]. The montage featured an excerpt of "Appassionata" from ''[[The Passage (1979 film)|The Passage]]'' composed by Michael J. Lewis.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|pp=173–174}}</ref>
